en: The Questions of Milinda: The Section on the Refutation of the Puzzles (Meṇḍakapañha),
Chapter on What is Set Aside.
10. The Question on Praising “Venerable Nāgasena, this was said by the Blessed One:
‘Monks, others might praise me, or they might praise the Dhamma, or they might praise the Saṅgha.’”
"In this matter, you should not feel joy, nor gladness, nor mental elation. Yet,
when the Tathāgata’s true praise was being spoken by the brahmin Sela, he became joyful, glad, and elated,
and further proclaimed his own qualities even more highly.
“I am the king, O Sela,
the unsurpassed King of Dharma;
by means of Dharma I turn the wheel.”
‘The wheel is irreversible.
Yet, venerable Nāgasena, if it was said by the Blessed One:
‘Monks, whether others speak in praise of me, or speak in praise of the Dhamma, or speak in praise of the Saṅgha...’”
"In that regard, you should not feel joy, nor gladness, nor mental elation," yet when the true praise of the brahmin Sela was being spoken, he was joyful, glad, and elated,
and further proclaimed his own virtues even more; therefore, that statement is false.
If, when the true praise of the brahmin Sela was being spoken, he was delighted, joyful, and elated,
and further proclaimed his own virtues, then in that case, monks,
you should not feel joy or gladness if others speak in praise of me, or if they speak in praise of the Dhamma or the Saṅgha.
‘One should not allow the mind to become elated’—that statement also is false.
This too is a double-pronged question that has come to you; it must be resolved by you.
“It was indeed spoken, Great King, by the Blessed One:”
“Monks, whether others should speak in praise of me, or speak in praise of the Dhamma or the Saṅgha, you should not feel joy, nor rapture, nor elation of heart.
And while the true praise of the brahmin Sela was being spoken, he further proclaimed his own virtues:
“I am King Sela,” he said.
“I am the unsurpassed King of Dhamma;
by means of the Dhamma I turn the wheel,
a wheel that cannot be turned back.”
"First, Great King, when the Blessed One was elucidating the true nature, essence, and characteristic of the Dhamma—which is its own nature, unerring, real, factual, and suchness—he said:
'Monks, whether others speak in praise of me, or speak in praise of the Dhamma, or speak in praise of the Saṅgha, you should not therein feel delight, nor joy, nor mental exultation.'"
Furthermore, when the Blessed One was speaking words of praise according to reality for the brahmin Sela, he further proclaimed his own qualities:

“I am a king, O Sela; I am an unsurpassed Dhamma-king. This was not for the sake of gain, nor for the sake of fame, nor for his own sake, nor for the sake of a faction, nor out of a desire for disciples;
rather, it was out of compassion, with kindness, and for the sake of their welfare.
“...there will be for him the realization of the Dhamma, as well as for three hundred young brahmins. Thus he spoke further of his own excellence:
“I am a king, O Sela, an unsurpassed King of Dhamma.
“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena! It is so; thus I accept it.”
The tenth question: On the Description of Praise.
